clue.text: Guides beginning climbing amid fearsome heights

indicators.note: amid tells us the starting letter sits in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: fearsome means dire, dreadful
tors are rocky hills or heights, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of the word climbing

explanation.surface: Mountain guides start an ascent among terrifying peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the first letter of 'climbing', goes 'amid' DIRE + TORS. A tor is a rocky hilltop, a word common in the West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Directors steer and lead others, which is what guides do.

clue.text: It need not give rise to delay

indicators.note: give rise to tells us the letters of it need not produce something new

explanation.surface: It need not hold anything up.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is a holding back, so a hold-up or delay, as of a pupil kept late.

clue.text: Perch — very large — in decay

indicators.note: in puts the size abbreviation within the word for decay

parts.note: rot is decay
OS is outsize, a clothing size meaning very large

explanation.surface: A huge, rotting perch.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds perch.

clue.text: Provides food outside the church for those successful in the field

indicators.note: outside means the word for provides food wraps round the church abbreviation

parts.note: to cater is to provide food

explanation.surface: Caterers set up outside the church for the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders who hold catches are successful in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchers are fielders who take catches, dismissing batsmen.

clue.text: Not in favour of work with modelling

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posing is modelling for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes having a job that involves sitting for artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing means against, set in opposition.

clue.text: The mark put on a sailor was a sacred symbol

indicators.note: put on, in a down clue, places the mark above the sailor

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman's tattoo was a holy emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was a sacred emblem in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: A trainee going before a member gets a warning

indicators.note: going before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the limb in the across entry

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate a trainee driver displays
an arm is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: A new recruit outranked by a senior colleague receives a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal of danger, a kind of warning.

clue.text: He's a household god, being over one hundred

indicators.note: being over, in a down clue, sets the god above the numerals

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A man is worshipped at home despite being over a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' splits as He + is: the definition is 'He', the Visigoth king who sacked Rome in 410.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaric was a Visigoth king, a man named by the pronoun.

clue.text: Rather slow and steady worker in love

parts.note: the ant is proverbially a diligent, steady worker
love is nil, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A slow, plodding employee is in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, slightly lighter than andante, at a moderate pace.

clue.text: Sound bird, though that's not really important

indicators.note: sound says the bird's name is said aloud

parts.note: the mynah is a talking bird of the starling family

explanation.surface: A healthy bird, though not one of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' seems to mean healthy, but it signals the homophone; in British speech mynah and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor means lesser, of little significance.

clue.text: Unusually wet spot to hold a dance

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of wet spot are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A damp patch on the floor contains a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in quick march time.

clue.text: A group of musicians on leave

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Some musicians are away on leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is to leave it behind for good, a synonym when read as a verb.

clue.text: The cut in pay that's not challenged

indicators.note: that's reads as that has, the phrase holding the run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: An unopposed reduction in wages goes through.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap in 'not challenged'; 'The' and 'in pay' only dress the surface of a pay cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut or nick.

clue.text: A tradesman may burst into tears

indicators.note: may burst suggests the letters of into tears breaking apart and re-forming

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper might break down crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper and pens, a kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Split on trendy male — it's natural

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the word for split after the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
he is the male pronoun
rent means torn, split

explanation.surface: A fashionable man's clothes have torn; that's only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the order signal: in an across entry, the piece placed on another comes after it, so the word for split is written last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherent is built-in, innate, part of a thing's nature.

clue.text: Passes over some fish as a goodwill gesture

parts.note: hands means passes over, gives
hake is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Someone gives away fish to show kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaking hands is a gesture of friendship or agreement.

clue.text: Choose a table

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to please or choose, as in 'the wind bloweth where it listeth'
a table of items set out in order

explanation.definitionFit: Archaic 'list' means wish or choose; a list as noun is a catalogue or schedule.

clue.text: The person with money gets more confident after rate adjustment

indicators.note: after puts the comparative word beneath the rearranged letters
adjustment means the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more confident

explanation.surface: The moneyed man feels better after interest rates change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' is the anagram signal for the word rate alone; 'after' places the comparative last, giving TREA then the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer keeps and manages an organisation's funds.

clue.text: Replaced stock in a strong colour

indicators.note: in puts the word for stock inside the word for the colour

parts.note: red is a strong colour
a store is a stock or supply

explanation.surface: Goods put back on the shelf are in a bold shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Restored means put back, returned to place.

clue.text: Taking a great number in flight is irresponsible conduct

indicators.note: in places the article and numeral inside the word for flight

parts.note: an escape is a flight from danger
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a great number

explanation.surface: Many joining in an escape is reckless behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a reckless adventure or prank.

clue.text: Such a figure could make one cross

definitions.text: Such a figure could make one cross

parts.words: Such a figure could make one cross
parts.note: in Roman numerals one followed by a cross (an X) makes this number

explanation.surface: A certain person could make anyone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the X shape: I then X is the Roman numeral IX.
explanation.definitionFit: IX, one and the cross-shaped ten, is the Roman form of this numeral.

clue.text: Beach shoes are quite wrong here!

indicators.note: quite wrong says the letters of shoes are must be put in another order

explanation.surface: Shoes are unsuitable on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The seashore is the strip of land by the sea, a beach.

clue.text: Unqualified — ran into craft

indicators.note: into means ran goes inside the word for craft

parts.note: art is skill, craft

explanation.surface: An unskilled worker barged into a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter, out-and-out, without qualification.

clue.text: Bedding for the family?

definitions.meaning: straw or similar material put down for animals to sleep on
a brood of young born to an animal at one time

explanation.definitionFit: Litter is straw bedding for animals and also a brood of puppies or kittens.

clue.text: Lack of liberty and aim in retirement

indicators.note: in places the word for aim within the word for retirement

parts.note: rest is retirement, withdrawal from activity
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: Being confined goes hand in hand with ambitions in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is confinement or restriction, the absence of freedom.

clue.text: Study Eastern novelist

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone studies an oriental writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Simpletons taken for a ride?

definitions.meaning: donkeys are animals people ride, as on a beach

explanation.definitionFit: Asses are both fools and donkeys, the beasts given rides on.

clue.text: A flighty creature appearing lit-up in the roadway

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a roadway

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word lit is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A giddy animal shows up drunk in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word lit, giving TIL; 'flighty' sounds like fickle but means able to fly: the stilt is a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilt is a wading bird, so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Primitive man, a six-footer — so unyielding

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible
an ant is an insect, which has six feet

explanation.surface: A primeval man of great height refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means firmly resolved, refusing to give way.

clue.text: Prompter is stern about exit

indicators.note: about means the word for stern goes round the word for exit

parts.note: the rear is the stern, the back of a ship
to exit is to die, as a player's stage exit from life

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter speaks sternly about an actor leaving the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompter' looks like a theatre job but is the comparative of prompt.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier means quicker or more willing, i.e. more prompt.

clue.text: An occasion for uniform with a casual sort of shirt

parts.note: even means regular, uniform
a T-shirt is a casual shirt

explanation.surface: A dress-uniform function where an informal shirt is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening, an occasion.

clue.text: Leftists always hold a nondrinker to be quite a dog!

parts.note: reds are communists, leftists

indicators.note: hold says the word for always contains the abstainer

parts.note: e'er is a poetic form of ever, always
TT is teetotal, a nondrinker

explanation.surface: Left-wing types always regard an abstainer as a real cur.
explanation.walkthrough: A red setter is the Irish setter, a gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter is a breed of gun dog, so quite a fine hound.
